main_text.l: LATINUS Laurentum Rex,Fauni & Maricæ, filius fuit.
Hic vel bello ab Ænea victus, vel tantùm certior factus quís-
nam,& unde esset Æneas,antequam signa canerent,ipsi Ænea
dextram,fidei signum,dedit:filiam deinde in uxorem tradidit,
quanquam prius pacta esset Turno Rutulorum regi.Æneas de
nomine uxoris Lauiniæ, Lauinium appellat. Turnus ob præ-re-
ptam Lauiniam sibi pactam , bellum mouet: utrinque summa
contentione pugnatum est: inclinauit tamen victoria in Tro-
ianos , qui Latinum eo in prælio amisere, anno mundi 2787.
ante Christum natum 1175. Titus Liuius lib.1. & Diony. Ha-
LAVINIA Latini & Amatæ filia, Æneæ uxor post Creu-
sam fuit. Hæc mortuo Ænea Ascanij tutelam gessit: deinde ab
eodem Ascanio, Lauinio, urbe iam florente atque opulenta,
donata est:nouā.ipse[?] aliam sub Albano monte condidit, quam
ab situ porrectæ in dorso urbis, Longam Albam appellauit.
Titus Liuius lib.1. Lauinia Syluium Posthumum peperit ter-
tium regem Latinorum: qui sic dictus est,quòd post patris Æ-
neæ fatum in syluis natus ac educatus sit. Videto ut supra.

page.notes: Two engraved coin medallions above the text, not transcribed as printed text. Left coin legend: LATINVS (curved, left side) and AMATA (right side), showing two profile heads. Right coin legend: LAVINIA, showing a female profile head. Printer's ornament (decorative cartouche with a mask) below the text, not transcribed. "nouā.ipse": the a carries a macron, read with uncertainty. Spelling u/v changed per rules in running text: uxor, unde, utrinque, ut, urbe, urbis; capitals LATINUS (vowel U). The paragraph beginning "LAVINIA" opens with a capitalised name in other type, so it is kept as a paragraph, not a heading.
